# Help & Version Reference

What `glassfrog` produces when you ask it to describe itself or report its
version.

## Overview

Help & Version is the read-only presentation surface of the CLI. Help text is
produced by the command framework's standard rendering over the registered
command set; this reference fixes which invocations produce which kind of
output, not the byte-exact layout. All output here is a **success** outcome on
**standard output**.

## Invocations

| Invocation | Output |
|---|---|
| `glassfrog --help` *(or bare `glassfrog`, routed by dispatch)* | Root **listing**: the program summary, then top-level commands and groups — each with its one-line summary — in alphabetical order by name. |
| `glassfrog <group> --help` *(or bare `glassfrog <group>`)* | Group **listing**: the group's usage line and summary, then its immediate child commands/subgroups with summaries, alphabetically. Immediate children only — not recursive. |
| `glassfrog <path> --help` *(leaf)* | Leaf **usage**: the command's usage/invocation line, its one-line summary, and its flags (framework-standard form). |
| `glassfrog --version` | The CLI **version string alone** (e.g. `1.2.0`) — the bare value, not a `glassfrog version 1.2.0` template. |
| `glassfrog version` | The **same** version string as `--version` — identical output. |

## Flags and commands

| Name | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--help` | flag | The framework's built-in help flag, available on every command/group/root. Requests help/usage for the command it is attached to. |
| `--version` | root flag | Requests the version string. |
| `version` | leaf command | Requests the version string; output identical to `--version`. |

**Hidden built-ins**: the framework's auto-injected `help` and `completion`
*commands* are hidden — they appear in no listing, and `glassfrog help` /
`glassfrog completion` do not resolve as built-in commands. The `--help` *flag*
remains available everywhere.

## Behavior

- **Requesting help**: via the `--help` flag on any command/group/root, or by
  dispatch routing a bare group or bare root to the listing outcome. There is no
  standalone `help` command.
- **Listing order**: commands within any listing are alphabetical by name —
  stable across runs, so output is byte-for-byte identical for an unchanged
  command set and a command can be located by name.
- **Group vs leaf**: a leaf's `--help` shows its usage; a group's `--help` shows
  the listing of its immediate children.
- **Version parity**: `--version` and the `version` command read one underlying
  version value and emit the same bare line; build tooling sets the value at
  compile time.
- **Precedence**: when both `--help` and `--version` are supplied, **help** is
  produced.
- **Empty command set**: `glassfrog --help` produces a coherent listing that
  names no commands rather than failing.
- **Version-unset fallback**: when no version is stamped into the build, the
  version output is the placeholder `0.0.0-dev` rather than an empty string. A
  build stamps the real version via `-ldflags "-X …/internal/cli.version=<value>"`.

## Boundaries

| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `glassfrog bogus --help` (unregistered path) | Renders **nothing** for `bogus` — an unrecognized command is Argument Dispatch's unknown-command contract (message on stderr). |
| `glassfrog roles --version` (`--version` on a non-root command) | Not a version request; the unrecognized flag is dispatch/parsing's usage error. |
| Exit codes | Out of scope here — mapping any outcome to a code is the [Exit-Code Convention](exit-code-convention.md). |
| Structured/JSON output | Not produced — out of scope for the skeleton. |

## Related

- Command names and summaries come from the registered command set (Command
  Registration); the registration guard guarantees every command has a non-empty
  summary to show.
- The accompanying process exit code is set by the
  [Exit-Code Convention](exit-code-convention.md) (help/listing/version are
  `Success` → `0`).
